Can anyone tell me if this method of lifting has worked for them?

I think it's probably worth trying. From my experience many programs focus on fully engaging muscle fibers and maxing out or working to failure. Rather than saying the number of workouts is meaningless, other programs focus on giving ample time for muscles worked to "recover" before working them again. One thing in the article that stuck or to me was the part about untrained individuals seeing muscle growth in 3 weeks. Many programs can claim results in this area, I believe, because growth will be seen quickly in any untrained individual. Similarly, very overweight individuals can see rapid weight loss quickly and early when diet is modified and exercise, over time this will slow or normalize. This is to say that it seems a weight lifting program can yield early gains, but how consistent are they over time? I would prefer consistent growth or change to quick or early results that drop off. I saw a routine a while ago, that was designed for people going on a cruise or similar vacation. It was claiming that you follow the routine for 3 weeks or a month leading up to your trip, the benefit being that your muscles continued growing while on the week vacation, with no work while vacationing.
